lessons.title: The CCP is a web app with a telephone inside
lessons.why: Sign-in can succeed when media cannot. Those are different allow lists.
paras: Signaling and the UI use TCP 443 to the instance, CloudFront, and the transport domains. Media uses UDP 3478 to TurnNlb. The docs recommend Option 1, the domain list, and ask you to test more than 200 calls.
VDI and VPN are the usual reasons a lab works and the floor does not. Media should go directly to AWS.
points: Supported browsers only. A locked-down browser without WebRTC permissions fails closed.
Headsets with their own DSP can still be fine. Browser permission for the microphone is not optional.
The Endpoint Connectivity tool is the first test, before a packet capture.
Stateless firewalls need ephemeral UDP back in.
lessons.mistake: Blaming the carrier for a softphone that never established ICE.

lessons.title: The workspace is where the ecosystem becomes visible
lessons.why: Profiles, cases, views, and third-party apps belong here, not in a second monitor full of URLs.
paras: The agent workspace can host step-by-step guides through Show view, third-party applications, Customer Profiles, and Cases. A screen pop is a view or an app that reads the contact attributes.
Screen recording, where you enable it, is a separate charge on the Basic list at 0.006 USD per minute and a privacy decision you document.
points: Give agents one place to see the attribute you collected.
Views are configuration, not a custom CCP.
A custom CCP using Streams is justified when the workspace cannot host the system of record.
ACW is part of the handle time the WFM tool must see.
lessons.mistake: Training agents to paste the phone number into the CRM by hand.

number.n: Workspace, unless Streams is truly required

lessons.title: Streams is the supported way to embed the CCP
lessons.why: If you must hide the CCP inside another app, use amazon-connect-streams. Do not scrape the page.
paras: The library initializes a CCP iframe, then emits agent and contact events. You can run it media-less, which is useful for a supervisor wall and useless as a phone. Softphone options have to be turned on for audio, and the host page has to be on the approved origin.
The GitHub repository is amazon-connect/amazon-connect-streams. Read its event list. Login, contact incoming, connected, and ended are the ones a screen pop needs.
points: Init once. A second init on navigation is a classic bug.
Do not store the agent's password in your app. Use SAML.
Media still needs UDP 3478. The library does not tunnel it.
lessons.mistake: An iframe of the admin website as a shortcut.

lessons.title: VDI, VPN, and the audio path
lessons.why: The browser that runs the CCP must be the browser whose network can reach TURN.
paras: If the CCP runs inside a data-center VDI, media comes from the data center, not from the headset's house. That adds latency and often blocks UDP. Video calling is documented as unsupported in VDI.

The network troubleshooting page lists firewalls, NAT, and VPNs as the first causes of quality and disconnects. Prefer a direct path. Use the Endpoint Connectivity tool on the same desktop the agent uses.
points: One-way audio is often NAT or a stateful rule that never saw the return traffic.
Jitter and loss show up as robotic audio, not as a flow error.
Do not stack a VPN, a proxy, and VDI and then tune the flow.
Remote agents need the same allow list as the office.
lessons.mistake: Testing on a home laptop and rolling out to a locked VDI fleet.
